patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient has been brought to the emergency department by her brother due to severe chest pain. She is grieving the recent loss of her husband in a car accident and is still in a state of shock over the event.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: No significant past medical history provided.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Non-smoker. No history of alcohol or drug abuse. Recently widowed.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies recent illness, fever, or cough.

questions: Is the chest pain worse when you take a deep breath (pleuritic)?
Do you have any fever or night sweats, or have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes (e.g., in your neck or groin)?
Have you noticed any new mouth sores, genital ulcers, or other rash lesions elsewhere on your body (especially on the hands/feet or trunk)?
Have you noticed any easy bruising or bleeding (e.g., frequent nosebleeds, gum bleeding, or petechiae) and do you know your recent blood counts (CBC) results?
Are the thigh bumps purple/red and do they flatten under pressure (non-blanching), or are they flesh-colored and blanch normally?
Are the bumps tender, have they grown or changed quickly, and do they have any scale or a central plug (like a “dimple” or keratin core)?
Have you noticed any central “dimple” or keratin plug in the middle of the bumps?
Are the bumps rough/“stuck-on” or do any have a central keratin plug or crater (when you look up close or feel them)?
When you look up close at a few of the bumps, do any have a central keratin-filled crater/“plug” that can be scraped out (like keratoacanthoma)?
Have you noticed any involvement of the palms/soles or any rash on the trunk or around the mouth/eyes?
answers: Doctor: Is the chest pain worse when you take a deep breath (pleuritic)? Patient: I’m not having any chest pain at all. My main issue has been small, non-itchy bumps on my left thigh for about three weeks, along with fatigue and general malaise for a few months.
I haven’t had any fever or night sweats. I don’t recall any swollen lymph nodes in my neck or groin.
“No, I haven’t noticed any mouth sores or genital ulcers. I also haven’t seen other rash lesions on my hands, feet, or trunk—just the small, non-itchy bumps on my left thigh.”
I haven’t had easy bruising or bleeding—no frequent nosebleeds or gum bleeding, and I haven’t noticed petechiae. I don’t know my recent blood counts or CBC results.

I haven’t noticed them being purple or red, and they don’t seem to be non-blanching—more like small flesh-colored bumps that don’t itch. I’m not sure if they flatten under pressure because I haven’t tested that carefully.
Patient: They aren’t tender, and I’d say they’ve slowly appeared over the last three weeks without quickly changing. I haven’t noticed any scaling or a central dimple/plug in any of the bumps.
I haven’t noticed any central dimple or keratin plug in the middle of the bumps. They look like small flesh-colored, non-itchy bumps on my left thigh that have slowly appeared over about three weeks.
They don’t feel rough or “stuck-on” to me, and when I look up close I haven’t noticed any central keratin plug or crater. They just seem like small, flesh-colored, non-itchy bumps on my left thigh.
“I haven’t noticed any central keratin-filled crater or plug that could be scraped out, and the bumps don’t look rough or crater-like—just small flesh-colored, non-itchy bumps on my left thigh.”
“No, I haven’t noticed any rash on my palms or soles, and nothing around my mouth or eyes. I also haven’t seen any rash on my trunk—just the small, non-itchy bumps on my left thigh.”
